t: This is the Coronet in Notting Hill, a theatre in a building from 1898. For ninety years of the last century it worked as a cinema, from 1923 until 2013. In 2014 a neighbouring company, The Print Room, bought it and turned it back into a theatre. Today it stages plays, dance, poetry, film and music, often lesser-known work by classic authors alongside new writing. It has a main auditorium and a smaller black box space. The architect was W. G. R. Sprague, who designed at least thirty-five theatres and was apprenticed to Frank Matcham.
